dogOwnership.unit: percent of surveyed dog owners / possession respondents in Paris agglomeration, as described by FACCO
dogOwnership.quote: un taux de possession qui chute à 25% dans les grandes villes et même 22% dans l’agglomération parisienne
dogOwnership.modelTransfer: Applied to local households as an explicit proxy; not a measured Châtillon household rate

behavior.notes: Simulated urinary events, including marking and elimination without distinguishing them; no measured door preference.

reference.defecationUse: Historical short-observation rate, no longer linearly extrapolated to full-day defecation counts

behavior.modelTransfer: Urination observational mean extrapolated to walks with expected pause time accounted for; not a local calibration or clinical norm. Poisson arrivals and uniform individual factor 0.5 to 1.5 are unvalidated modeling assumptions. Illustrative pauses are not clinically measured urination durations.
behavior.defecationNotes: Daily per-dog Poisson count allocated among outings in proportion to actual moving duration. More or longer walks do not increase the daily expected count. Slider 0 to 4 is a scenario range, not a clinical maximum; no individual hard cap. These are events during public walks; private-garden elimination and fecal collection are not modeled. Mean, Poisson distribution and pause duration are assumptions, not locally calibrated medical norms.

additionalReferences.use: Evidence of contextual variability, not a local rate calibration
Evidence of sex, maturity and handler effects in shelter dogs; no numeric coefficients transferred

additionalReferences.institution: UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine
additionalReferences.use: Distinguish social urine marking from bladder emptying; no urine volume inferred

behavior.durationStatus: 25 min is an adjustable target scenario setting, not a measured urban or Chatillon mean; attained average reported separately

walkingReferences.title: Associations between Neighborhood Disadvantage and Dog Walking among Participants in the Dog Aging Project
walkingReferences.limits: US volunteer sample, not exclusively urban; no direct transfer to Châtillon
Weekly totals in dog walkers, not directly measured mean duration per outing
Japanese dense built environment associations, no local duration or elimination-rate calibration

behavior.durationMinutesMeaning: Target duration; achieved trip duration is distance / individual moving speed + sampled pauses
behavior.scheduleNotes: Minimum rest interval enforced between outings of each dog including the midnight boundary; modeling constraint, not a veterinary recommendation
behavior.routeSelection: Closest target duration among up to six candidate connected loops; achieved mean duration and distance reported

defecationReferences.title: Apparent total tract nutrient digestibility and metabolizable energy estimation in commercial fresh and extruded dry kibble dog foods
defecationReferences.limits: Small short dietary cohorts; diet-sensitive frequency, not a clinical reference interval or calibration of public-walk events in Chatillon

defecationReferences.title: Effects of microalgae as dietary supplement on palatability, digestibility, fecal metabolites, and microbiota in healthy dogs
defecationReferences.limits: Adult Beagle dietary trials; selected diet means, not population limits or a public-walk calibration

dailyHeat.aggregation: Weighted elimination events in [00:00, selected time), periodically assigned to a 24 h day
dailyHeat.normalization: Normalized compact kernel; color maximum fixed to complete-day maximum for selected scenario and event type, recalculated when either changes. Equal colors are not equal absolute quantities across scenarios.
dailyHeat.urbanism: Residential surface times levels weights departures; accessible street network constrains routes. No clinically validated park, tree, facade or paving multiplier.
dailyHeat.meaning: Theoretical event concentration, not measured contamination, urine volume, health risk, or abandoned feces

observationPrecision: 5 m is a geometric query radius on simulated sampled routes, not a guarantee of positional or statistical accuracy; OSM completeness and the weighted sample limit interpretation
reproducibility: CSV exports scenario settings and seed. Exact reproduction also requires identical geographic data and simulator version.
